Baltimore, whats the story ? Quick rundown please

As happens often, a form of social protest has evolved into an urban war zone punctuated by opportunism.

**The Background and the Mysterious Death of Freddie Gray

On April 12 at 8:39 AM, Freddie Gray was talking to a friend on the street when he was approached by three police officers on bicycles. Media reports differ as to the details of his past, but we know he lived with his sisters in a shitty area in Baltimore. According to police, he attempted to flee "unprovoked" (what this means I am admittedly unsure) and was taken into custody. He had a knife, although it has never been reported that he was attempting to use it against the officers, but rather was just in his possession. Also enflaming protestors, he weighed 145 lbs, so the "he was huge and scary" defense that may have at least somewhat explained a use of excessive force in the Eric Garner and Michael Brown (perhaps rightfully here, based on what little I know) cases was not applicable here.

At some point during this altercation, his spinal cord was "80% severed" at the neck. This is where the story of police definitively varies from witnesses. Officer Garrett Miller claims that Gray was "arrested without force or incident" but witnesses, as well as medical reality, obviously dispute this. After collapsing into a coma, he died on April 19.

**Protests Begin

On April 21, peaceful protests proper began, but protesters were antagonized in the media by the police union, and, ironically, likened to a lynch mob. (See also: The Root, NYTimes ).

Eventually, the Baltimore PD suspended six officers in connection with Gray's death. The police commissioner acknowledged that officers didn't do a sufficient job to help him medically.

**Shit Goes Down

After five days of peaceful protests, violence began on April 25. It really properly began yesterday, April 27. The Governor of Maryland declared a state of emergency and the National Guard were called in. This is where people who weren't already aware of the story, including myself, started hearing about it. As happened in New Orleans during Katrina, or in Vancouver after the Canucks lost in the Stanley Cup Final in 2010, or during the Rodney King riots in 1992, the sociopolitical implications of a peaceful movement allowed impoverished or otherwise disaffected individuals to selfishly abuse a state of heightened tension.

**My Editorializing

The switchblade thing is a non-issue, mostly because it's so nebulous as to what is a switchblade versus what is a "magic-assist" knife. For instance, I own one of these, which is almost identical in form and function to a switchblade, and is extremely sharp. A 4.3" blade this sharp could very easily kill a man, but it cost me barely more than $30 on Amazon. Furthermore, I'm in Canada, which has weapons restriction laws that aren't much less restrictive than the Third Reich's, and they're still common here.

People care more about this than previous cases because, frankly, the only "mainstream" case that compares in terms of seemingly unwarranted excessive police force was the Eric Garner case, and even then, Garner was a large man (albeit as much a victim as Freddie Gray), nowhere near as easy to apprehend than relatively tiny Gray.

As much as Redditors might like to pretend that we live in a post-race society, that's such a laughable notion for a slew of reasons, not the least of which that whether or not overt, anvilicious "To Kill a Mockingbird"-style skin colour-based racism exists is totally irrelevant. All that matters is that certain minorities, primarily black and indigenous Americans, are totally and systemically economically marginalized (as are lots of segments of the white population, they just aren't as prevalent proportionally or as densely concentrated in certain areas, so they don't get as much attention; that doesn't mean that they shouldn't). Race is now largely a proxy for class. Classism is worse than "racism" in the traditional sense, in terms of how minorities are affected. I'm all for national and international dialogues about race, as well as sexuality and gender, but ultimately those are a means to an end. What we actually need are discussions about social and economic stratification. Race and gender play into that discussion, but not nearly as much as that discussion plays into race and gender.

These riots are awful and I hope those who commit violent crimes are apprehended and prosecuted under the full extent of the law. At the same time, I agree, the antics of so-called "Tumblrinas" are selfish, crazy, and often not based in any semblance of reality. But there is every valid reason for peaceful protest and political action in this case.

In this case, as well as in terms of social and political discussions, it's always the biggest assholes who yell the loudest and are the most visible, and because of the nature of how the internet and mass media works, it's always the most extreme people who get the most airtime and, unfortunately, become most associated with the movement that they're a part of (or, in some cases, only seek to). I bet most users probably aren't even aware that radical centrism is a political position? Compare the number of times you've heard the phrase "radical centre" to "radical fascist" or "radical socialist." Every time you hear the word "thug" as a substitute for the word "nigger," you've seen an example of how class has usurped racism in its traditional form as our society's preferred form of discrimination. Or even our society's preferred form of racism.
